I'm kind of cheating: I have a host on a static IP running my own mail, web, and DNS servers. An advantage is that I can create a new email address to use in about 5 seconds, so I use a unique email address for every company I do business with. If I start getting spammed, I immediately know which company got broken into or sold my address.

If you can tolerate installing OSes and reading documentation and fiddling around with configuration files, it's surprisingly easy to start playing around with running your own servers. Almost any dirt-cheap PC will work, even if it's 8 years old with unimpressive specs because servers just handling your own stuff don't need fast CPUs or big memory or fast graphics. What you do is pick a Linux distribution like Debian or Fedora Server if you're not afraid of command lines, or Ubuntu or Mint if you're new to Linux and want to ease into it with something more desktoppy. Once you've got that rolling, then it's like "Hey! It doesn't matter if I break this thing! I can wipe it and reinstall all I want." Then use your favorite search engine on things like "how do I set up a mail server on linux" and you'll get pages like http://arstechnica.com/information-technology/2014/02/how-to-run-your-own-e-mail-server-with-your-own-domain-part-1/ and entire weekends will evaporate like never before.

This is a novel by Tang Jia San Shao translated from Chinese to English by a TLer named 'Bagelson'. In the Chinese rankings, I believe that this is rated in the top 5 of all the novels in it's genre. It is definitely the best story on /r/LightNovels or /v/Lightnovels.

This is a story about Tang San, who steals and secretly learns the pinnacle techniques of the Tang Sect's hidden weapons and poisons. After revealing what he has done he commits suicide, but is instead transported to another world as a newborn. He develops at a frightening pace in this new world, growing in strength and developing bonds with his friends and family. It is very well written, and very well translated. If you like martial arts or first person fantasy, then this is a must read.

It is not fully translated yet, but Bagelson continues to translate at a frightening pace.
